ideal: Nf3 misses Qh5, whose threat of Qxf7# lets White take the e5-pawn after g6.
note: The f7 mate threat makes the pawn-winning queen move work.

ideal: f3 misses Qxd8+ Kxd8, drawing the king away from f7 so Nxf7+ forks the king and h8-rook.
note: The king deflection wins material; losing castling rights is secondary.

ideal: d5 lets exd5 and dxe6 take both central pawns while Bg6+ drives the king to f8.
note: Black loses both central pawns and leaves the king unable to castle.

ideal: Qe3 loses the queen to the checking fork Nc2+ followed by Nxe3+.
note: The royal fork is decisive; the loss of castling rights adds little.

ideal: Qa8+ allows Qg4, threatening Qxg2# and driving the king into the open after Kf1 Qxg2+.
note: The g2-pawn is part of a mating attack, not the main prize.

ideal: Qxe6+ misses Ba3, whose Qxf8# threat forces Rf7 and lets Nxf7 win the exchange.
note: The bishop move creates the mate threat that makes the rook vulnerable.

ideal: Bxc1 allows Ng7+, forking the king and queen and winning the queen for a knight after Nxf5 Nxf5.
note: The checking fork wins the queen; the bishops on c1 also cancel out.

ideal: h3 misses Bxf7+ Kd7, winning the f7-pawn and leaving the black king unable to castle.
note: The bishop survives the check and later trades for the c6-knight.

ideal: Nxd6+ misses Bxd6 cxd6 Nxd6+, which forces Ke7 instead of letting Black castle.
note: Both move orders win a pawn, and the extra b7 capture is answered by Qxb2.

ideal: f3 misses Rb5 Nd7 Qxd7, winning the d7-knight.
note: The b7 mate threat appears after Qg6+ Kh2, not immediately after Rb5.

ideal: Bxe6 misses Rxe6 fxe6 Rxe6, when the threat of Re8# gives White time for Ra6+ and Rxa3.
note: The mate threat forces a defensive rook move before the a3-bishop falls.

ideal: Bxf4 allows Nxd4 and Nxc2+, losing the d4- and c2-pawns as the bishops and rooks are exchanged.
note: The material exchanges cancel except for the two white pawns.

ideal: Qf5 lets Ne4 attack the queen and take the d6-pawn with check after Qg6.
note: The pawn comes with tempo, whereas Black also moves the king in the best line.

ideal: c3 allows Bxf2+ Kd2, drawing the king into the centre and preventing castling.
note: The exposed king is the main damage; the best line also gives up the f-pawn.

ideal: Re1 loses the queen to Qxe2 because recapturing allows a back-rank mate.
note: The queen capture is protected tactically by the back-rank mating attack.

ideal: cxd3 misses Rh7, when the Qf7# threat persists after Bg5+ f4 and wins the bishop after Qf6 Qxg5.
note: Both cited positions threaten Qf7#, and the defensive queen move abandons the bishop.

ideal: h6 misses Bxf2+ Kxf2 Ng4+, regaining the bishop with Qxg5 and winning the f2-pawn.
note: The checking knight move opens the queen attack on g5 while White must answer check.

ideal: Kf7 allows Qh4, whose Qxh7# threat wins the b4-knight after h6 Qxb4.
note: Qh4 attacks the knight and threatens mate, so Black cannot save both.

ideal: d6 loses the f6-knight to Bxf6, threatening Bxg7# while a pawn recapture opens a fatal g-file attack.
note: The g7-pawn cannot safely recapture because that permits mate on g8.

ideal: Nc2 lets Nh4 and Nxf5 take the f5-bishop before the knight collects the a1-rook.
note: The castling-loss card substitutes a different continuation for the supplied line, in which Black castles.

ideal: Nxe4 allows Bxf7+ Kxf7 Qd5+, forking the king and e4-knight and winning a pawn after Qxe4.
note: After cancelling the e-pawns, Black gives up a knight and pawn for a bishop.

ideal: Rxb3 misses Qe7, threatening Qe1# and winning the queen for a rook after Qxb5 cxb5.
note: Qe7 threatens mate immediately, and that threat remains after cxb5.

ideal: Rd1 allows Qxf4, threatening Qxf3# and forcing the defence Qe2 before Black takes the c5-bishop.
note: The pawn capture starts a forcing attack that also wins the bishop.

ideal: Qg2+ hangs the queen to Bxg2 instead of winning the c6-bishop with Nxc6.
note: The best line threatens mate first on g2 and then on f3, while winning a bishop and knight.

ideal: Ke8 allows Bxd5, winning a knight with a Qf7# threat before Bxc6+ trades the bishop for the other knight.
note: The material gain and the immediate mate threat are both real.

ideal: Rf8 loses the e6-pawn after Nxe6 Bxe6 Qxe6+, exchanging a bishop for a knight.
note: The extra pawn is the concrete gain; losing castling rights after trading queens is incidental.

ideal: hxg4 misses Nxc7+, which takes the queen with check.
note: The queen is won outright, making the castling detail irrelevant.

ideal: Qxc3+ misses Nf4, whose Qe2# threat wins the queen for a rook and knight after Qxf8+ Kxf8 Rf5+ Kg8 Rxf4.
note: The e2 mate threat is present at every cited stage and drives the material concession.

ideal: Qe7 allows Nxe5 and Bxd5, with the Qxb7# threat after Qb3 giving White time to capture the knight on e5.
note: The b7 mate threat is part of the sequence that makes the pawn gain stick.

ideal: Nc1 allows Rd2, threatening Rd1# and forcing Kf1 before Rd1+ Ke2 Rxc1 wins the knight.
note: The mate threat displaces the king and lets the rook take the c1-knight.
